one_sentence_story: When a jammed glass slide cast an accidental diagonal shadow in their 1958–1959 Johns Hopkins lab, David Hubel and Torsten Wiesel discovered that primary visual cortex (V1) ignores flat light spots and decomposes the visual world into oriented edges and columns — winning the 1981 Nobel Prize, saving children from amblyopia, and inspiring modern AI Convolutional Neural Networks.
so_what_for_you: Design slides, charts, and diagrams with crisp high-contrast edges and clean orientation lines rather than muddy gradients — you are speaking the native first language of primary visual cortex.
